key_insight: Continual learning for deepfake detectors can worsen demographic unfairness over time, so preserving accuracy alone is not enough.
engineering_relevance: For real-world security systems, model updates must be evaluated not just for robustness to new attacks but also for shifting fairness across demographic groups.
method: Evaluated continual-learning deepfake detectors on a chronological sequence of 11 real-world generation methods.
Tracked four fairness dimensions across diverse demographics and demographic intersections over time.
Compared CL families including rehearsal, prompts, and regularization to study performance–fairness tradeoffs.
evidence_signal: The study analyzes fairness metrics over time on 11 sequential deepfake generation methods, showing that accuracy drops often coincide with increased unfairness.
watch_item: Fairness gains were scarce and inequitable forgetting was not fully explained by underrepresentation, so mitigation may require changes to representation learning rather than only data balancing.
paper_title: Time to Fake It: Continual Machine Learning Intensifies Unfairness in Deepfake Detection
